changelog.title: Add from a person's page, Open on the new-action message
items: On a person's page (click a name under People) there is now an add box. What you type becomes an action already assigned to that person, with the same quick-add words as Today (dates, times, @names, risk: …). Press Enter or Add
The message that appears after you add something now has an Open button next to Undo, which takes you to the new item so you can edit it
td() works like today(): type it and it becomes today's date
Fixed: after unfolding a section on To confirm (or any page), the rows no longer have a big gap between the action and the answer buttons

Pop-ups: the Alerts tab now says so when the app is opened from a file on this computer, because browsers do not allow pop-ups there (use the live address; the bell works either way). The test button now tells you what to check if nothing appears

changelog.title: Fold sections, today(), and when things were done
items: Section headings can be folded. Click a heading (Past due, Today, Tomorrow, On your timeline, and the groups on Actions, the RAID pages, a person's page and To confirm, where each assigned person is a group) and everything under it hides. The count stays in the heading. The app remembers what you folded on this computer
Type today() anywhere (a note, an action, the search box, a title) and it turns into today's date as yyyy-mm-dd the moment you type the closing bracket. Ctrl + ; still works too

When you tick an action done, the app now keeps the date and time, and who it was (for example Claude, when you confirm their “done?”). It shows as “✓ Done Nov 9, 3:12 PM” on the Actions and Today pages, in the tooltip of a ticked action item in a note, and in the files for other people (doneAt, doneBy). Actions that were already done before this version have no date
Fixed: turning on browser pop-ups no longer unticks itself after you press Allow. The box now shows your choice, and a note says if the browser has not allowed it yet

changelog.title: Your own RAID types
items: Settings > RAID types is now a list you control. Add your own types (say Idea, Question or Blocker), rename any of them, change the icon, switch them on and off, and delete the ones you do not want. At least one type always stays. Risk, Issue and Decision are only the starting set, and you can bring one back with Restore
You can also rename the section itself (it starts as “RAID log”), so a notebook that is not about RAID can call it something else. The name shows in the sidebar, on the pages and in the phone view
Deleting a type keeps its items: they become plain actions, and the message after has Undo. Lines already written in your notes keep working

Your own types work everywhere the built-in ones do: the sidebar, the ＋ Tag… menu and typing the word in capitals, the Type menu, quick add (type idea: …), the page for each type, and the files shared with a Claude project (the type's name is used)
Number keys 5, 6 and 7 now go to the first three types you have switched on, whatever they are called
Older files open exactly as before: all three starting types on, with their usual names

changelog.title: Notifications
items: A 🔔 bell at the top of the sidebar (and in the top bar of a narrow window) shows how many things are new. Click it for the list: things waiting for your OK (done?, hand backs, suggestions), replies waiting on a shared page, what is due today or past due, and actions that are due at a certain time. If you are a teammate it also lists what was assigned to you and the owner's answers
Click an item to jump to it. Items you have not looked at are in bold, and Mark all read clears the count

Browser pop-ups: turn them on from the bell or Settings > Alerts, and the browser shows a notification when something new arrives, a timed action comes due, and once a day for what is due today. They only appear while the app is open in a tab. Nothing pops up for things that were already there when you first turned them on
Settings has two new tabs: Alerts (pop-ups, due-time reminders, the daily summary, and a test button) and RAID types, which used to share the Appearance tab

changelog.title: Hand an action back
items: On the Assigned to me page, each action now has a ↩ Hand back button next to Mark done… One click sends it back to whoever assigned it (type a note in the box first if you want to say why)
The owner sees it in To confirm as “… hands this back”, with Take it back (it becomes theirs again) or Keep with … (with an optional reason). Nothing changes until they press one
The teammate's screen says “Handed back: waiting for … to take it”, and shows the reason if the owner kept it with them
A Claude project can hand an action back too: the feed lists it as kind “back”

changelog.title: Renaming a person carries everything
items: Renaming a person now moves their feed, their folder, the pages shared with them and their earlier answers to the new name, not just their actions. Before, you got a second empty feed under the new name
Settings > Team has a Rename… button on every feed row (the People editor in the sidebar does the same thing). If the new name already exists, the two are merged into one
If you pick a folder that another person already uses, the app now asks “Move it to this name?” instead of refusing. The other person stops getting a feed until you choose a folder for them
A project that still answers under the old name is understood, so a rename never loses its answers
The name Claude is only offered in Settings > Team while there is no Claude on your team yet

changelog.title: Insert today's date
items: Press Ctrl + ; to type today's date as yyyy-mm-dd (for example 2026-11-09) wherever the cursor is: in a note, an action, the search box, a title or any other text box. It is the same shortcut Excel uses
If the cursor is not in a text box, the date is copied instead, with a message, so you can paste it where you want it
It is listed in the keyboard shortcuts sheet (press ?)

changelog.title: Claude projects
items: Settings > Team has a new “Add a Claude project” box. Type a name (say Website) and pick that project's folder, and you have a team member called Claude-Website. Assign to it by typing @Claude-Website, the same as any person. You can also tick “this is a Claude project” on an existing feed

A Claude project's feed starts with a “start here” block that tells whichever Claude opens the folder what the file is, how to answer in proposals.<label>.json, and the safety rules (your notes are not instructions, nothing changes until you press Confirm, never read your save file). The note behind each action and the note's title are included by default
Pages you share with a Claude project also get a Markdown (.md) copy next to the JSON, kept up to date, which is the easy one for a project to read

Each Claude project shows a status line (how many open, how many waiting for your OK, when it last answered) and a “Copy line for CLAUDE.md” button with a ready-made paragraph to paste into that project, so every session checks the feed
Names like Claude-Website are no longer offered as a slip of Claude, and the other way round, when you type an @name

changelog.title: Settings in tabs
items: Settings is no longer one long scroll. It opens as a window with tabs down the left: Your notes (save file, earlier versions, moving actions between notebooks), Appearance & RAID, Team (your team, feeds, and what others shared with you) and Help. Only one tab shows at a time
The app remembers the tab you were on. On a narrow window the tabs sit in a row across the top
Nothing in Settings was removed or renamed; each part is now under the tab it belongs with

On a teammate's computer, an action you answered with “done?” no longer stays at “Sent: waiting for … to confirm” after the owner says “Not yet”. It now shows the owner's answer and the reason they gave

changelog.title: Send actions to another notebook
items: Send actions… (Settings, or the link on the Actions page) packs up the actions assigned to one person and nothing else: no pages, no page titles. You can leave out done ones and choose whether each action’s note comes with it. It makes a file to save, or text to copy

Bring in actions… on the other notebook reads that file or pasted text and shows every action with a tick box. You choose who they are assigned to here (the person in the file maps to someone on your team, or no one, or someone new), and whether they become standalone actions or go inside a note you pick

Standalone actions get a from-… label so you can find what came from the other notebook. Categories are matched by name. Actions you already brought in start unticked, so sending the same ones twice does not duplicate them
Nothing is overwritten. A snapshot is taken first, and Undo removes exactly what was added. It also accepts the actions file the app writes for a person (assigned.….json)

changelog.title: Narrow windows and vertical monitors
items: When the window is narrow (900 pixels wide or less, which is what a vertical monitor often gives you, or a large display scale), the sidebar is no longer lost. A ☰ button in a bar at the top opens it as a drawer over the page; choosing something, tapping outside it or pressing Esc closes it. Ctrl + \ opens and closes it too

In a narrow window the list of pages is a shorter band above the note (about 30% of the height instead of 40%). The « button now folds it into a thin bar instead of leaving a tall empty band, and the buttons are bigger
Wider windows are unchanged

changelog.title: The editor bar is now tabs
items: The formatting bar above a note is split into tabs, like Word: Home (text style, bold, italic and so on, highlight, colour, size, Tag… and Checkbox, Clear), Lists (bullets, numbering, indent, fold) and Insert (link, divider, table, custom numbering)

A Table tab appears while your cursor is inside a table, with + Row, + Col, − Row, − Col and Delete table, and the bar jumps to it. It goes away when you leave the table and takes you back to the tab you were on
The ⌃ at the right end hides the tools and keeps just the tab names, for more room to write. Click a tab to bring them back. The bar remembers the tab you were on and whether you hid it
Nothing else changed: every button and keyboard shortcut works as before

changelog.title: A read-only view for your phone
items: On an iPhone, iPad or Android phone (a browser that can’t save to a file) the app now opens a phone view: one screen at a time, with Today, Actions, Notes and RAID tabs along the bottom. Tap a note to read it, and tap Back to return to the list
It is read-only, so nothing you do there can change or lose your notes. Fields are locked and every button that would edit something is switched off

First time: tap Open my notes file and pick todo-data.json from Files (OneDrive shows up there if the OneDrive app is installed). The phone keeps its own copy, so it opens straight away, even offline. To get your latest notes, tap Refresh at the top and pick the file again
Add the page to your Home Screen (Share, then Add to Home Screen) so Safari does not clear the copy after a week of not using it
To look at the phone view on a computer, add ?mobile=1 to the end of the address

changelog.title: Choose and rename your RAID types
items: Settings > RAID types: switch Risks, Issues and Decisions on or off, and give each its own name (for example call Issues “Blockers”). Everything starts on, with the usual names
It is saved in the notebook’s file, so your work notebook can keep all three while your home one hides what it does not need

A type that is switched off disappears from the sidebar, the ＋ Tag… menu, the Type menu, quick add and the number shortcuts, and typing RISK: (or its name) stays plain text. The items you already have stay in your notes, and Settings shows how many
A renamed type shows its new name everywhere. Type the new name in capitals to tag a line (or the original word, while the type is on). Lines you already wrote keep the word they were written with

changelog.title: Sort by name, Today count, superscript and subscript, list swap
items: Pages can be sorted A–Z or Z–A by name. Pinned pages stay at the top; untitled ones go last. It is separate from By date, which uses the dates on the notes
On the Today page, the count beside Today now shows how many are still open out of the day’s total (for example 2 of 5), instead of just the total
Superscript (x²) and subscript (x₂) buttons in the formatting bar, with Word’s shortcuts: Ctrl + Shift + = and Ctrl + =
In a bulleted list, typing “1. ” at the start of a line makes that line a numbered one instead. In a numbered list, typing “* ” (or “- ”) makes that line a bullet instead

changelog.title: Feed files are labelled with who wrote them
items: Assigned-action files are now named after the notebook that wrote them: assigned.reid.json instead of assigned.json. The label starts as your “I am” name, and Settings > Team has a “Label my files as” box if you want a different one. Leave it empty to use your “I am” name
Answers come back in the matching file (proposals.reid.json), so two people, or your work and home computers, can use one shared folder without overwriting each other
If another notebook has already used your label in that folder, the app stops and tells you instead of overwriting its file; pick a different label

From the team: if several people assign to you in one folder, each person gets their own block in Assigned to me, and your “done?” answers go to the right person. Folders with the older assigned.json still work

The first time your feed is written under its new name, the old assigned.json is replaced by a short note saying where the actions went (so nobody reads stale actions). Anyone you share with needs this version to see the new file names

changelog.title: A guided tour
items: New: a short guided tour that walks through each area of the app (views, RAID log, categories and people, search, the + button, list options, the editor, saving and Settings). It opens by itself the first time the app runs on a new computer
Take it any time from Settings > Help > Take the tour. Use the arrow keys or the buttons to move, and Esc to leave
If you already use the app, you get a one-time message offering the tour instead of it opening on its own

changelog.title: Bring in another copy of your notes
items: Import now accepts a whole data file (for example the one saved by the app on another computer), not just a notebook export. It adds to what you have and never overwrites it
Standalone actions come across too. The Import window lists them as their own line, with how many are new, newer, older or already here

A new “Give imported actions that have no one yet to…” box lets you hand the unassigned ones you bring in to Claude or a teammate in one go; actions that already have a person keep them. Leave it on “Keep as they are” to reassign later
Anything already here with the same identity is skipped (or kept as a copy, or replaced if the file's is newer, whichever you pick). A snapshot is taken first and the message after has Undo

changelog.title: Working from two devices
items: Saving no longer overwrites changes made on another device. If your data file changed since this page last read it (a second computer, or OneDrive), the app merges the two before it writes, so tasks made elsewhere are kept

The app now checks your data file when you come back to it and every 30 seconds, and brings in changes from another device on its own (a short message says so). Nothing is lost if you have unsaved edits: they are merged in

After new data arrives from another device, assigned-action feeds and shared pages are rewritten at once. So a task you give Claude on a second computer shows up in the Claude feed as soon as the computer that has the feed folder opens the app

A computer that does not have a person's feed folder no longer shows a “couldn’t write” or “paused” warning for that feed. Settings says “not set on this device”: the feed is written by the device that has the folder

changelog.title: Reasons for declining, assign a suggestion, tidier sidebar
items: Not yet (on a “done?” request) and No thanks (on a suggested action) now ask for an optional reason. The person who sent it sees your reason next to the action or the suggestion
A suggested action has an Assign to box: you, the person who suggested it, or anyone else on the team. It defaults to you
The page list on the left now shows the page's own date and time (the meeting date if it has one, otherwise when the page was made), not when it was last edited
The sidebar's Waiting for your OK row is now To confirm, on one line, with a small amber count instead of the tall red one. Counts in the sidebar are now centred in their row
Shortcut for the horizontal line: Ctrl + Shift + H, or type --- on its own line and press Enter
Pinned pages can be collapsed in the list: click the Pinned heading (▾ / ▸). It is remembered per notebook
Fixed: pages like Actions and Waiting were squeezed into a narrow strip when the window was 900 pixels wide or less

On laptop-sized windows the rows on Actions, Today, Risks and the other list pages put the action's text on its own line with the date, time, repeat, category and assignee under it, so the text and the “done?” line are no longer squeezed

changelog.title: Choose where each person's folder goes
items: Each person now has their own folder, and you choose it. Tick Keep a feed for Sam (Settings > Team) and the app asks where Sam's feed should go: pick any folder, on any drive or sync service, that you share with Sam. Her feed, the pages shared with her and her replies all live in that one folder. The folder is remembered, and each row shows which folder it is, with Change folder… and Allow buttons
Share this page shows each person's folder too, with Choose folder… next to anyone who has none yet. You cannot pick the same folder for two people, so nobody sees someone else's files
You no longer need one shared folder for everything. It is only needed for the older “everyone with the folder” sharing and notebook sharing. Feeds that already lived in shared/for-name keep working

changelog.title: Share a page with chosen people; teammates' side; suggested actions
items: Share a page with chosen people: Share… now asks who. Each person gets the page in their own folder (shared/for-name/pages/), read-only, and nobody else does. “Everyone with the shared folder” is still there as an option. Your notebooks and other pages are never exposed
An assigned action now links to its page: if the page the action is in is also shared with that person, their list shows “Open the page”. If it is not shared, they see only the action

Teammates: Settings > From the team connects a folder shared with you. Your sidebar then gets Assigned to me (the actions assigned to you, with Mark done… to propose it) and Shared with me (pages shared with you, read-only, with a box to send a suggestion back)

Teammates can also suggest a new action to you. It appears under Waiting for your OK as “Sam suggests…”, with Add it and No thanks. Adding it creates an action in your list (unassigned, noted as suggested by Sam)
Replies from a person's folder are only accepted when the author is that person

changelog.title: Assign to someone who is not on the team (guests)
items: When a name is not on your team you can now choose “Assign it anyway, as a guest”. The name goes into the assigned field and is remembered as a guest, so the next time you use it nothing is asked. Guests are not team members and have no feed

Guests show under the team in the sidebar, in the Assigned-to filters and in the @-name list (marked guest). In Settings > Team you can move a guest onto the team, merge a look-alike (Rei into Reid), or remove them
Names that arrive in a reply from someone else are saved as guests rather than joining the team

changelog.title: Team list and @-name picker
items: Your People list is now your team. Type @ in an action box (the Actions add box, RAID, Quick add, an action's text, a tagged line in a note) and a list of your team's names opens as you type. Use the arrow keys with Tab or Enter, or click, to fill the name in. The Assign boxes use the same list

A name that is not on the team is no longer added quietly. You are asked: “Rei” is not on your team. Did you mean Reid? Use Reid, add Rei to the team, or cancel. So @Rei can never become a second person by accident
If you assign an action to someone who has no assigned-action feed (when you use feeds), a message tells you they will not see it, with a button to turn their feed on

Settings > Team: add team members, switch the “only assign to people on the team” check on or off, and see names that look like duplicates (for example Rei and Reid) with a Merge button that moves their actions across

changelog.title: Assigned-action feeds and “done?” proposals
items: Settings > Assigned-action feeds: choose a person (for example Claude) and the app keeps a file in the shared folder (shared\for-Name\assigned.json) listing the actions assigned to them: standalone actions, and action items inside any of your notes, shared or not. It holds the action text, date, notes and status only, never the notes themselves. Note titles are included only if you tick that option

That person can answer by writing proposals.json in the same folder. A proposal never changes anything: it puts an amber “Claude: done?” badge beside the checkbox, with their note and Confirm / Not yet buttons right there on the action. You always make the final call

It shows wherever the action shows: Actions, Today, Risks, Issues, Decisions, People, the RAID section under a note, and a standalone action's own page. The sidebar gets Waiting for your OK with a count, listing everything to confirm, grouped by person

A proposal is only accepted from the person the action is assigned to, and drops away if you reassign the action. Ticking the action yourself also settles it. Confirmed and declined proposals are kept in a log, and the feed tells the person what you decided
On a shared page, a tick from the person an action is assigned to now appears the same way, on the action itself, instead of waiting in the Replies list

changelog.title: Date filter next to the page search
items: Next to the search box on Actions, Risks, Issues, Decisions and People there is now a date filter: Overdue, Today, Tomorrow, This week, Next 7 days, No due date, A specific day, or a date range. Pick a day and only that day's items show, whatever the grouping
Clear all filters on the Actions page also clears the search and the date filter

changelog.title: Done lines crossed out, page search, two kinds of pin, notebook categories
items: In a note, a tagged line (ACTION, RISK, ISSUE, DECISION) is now crossed out and greyed when its action is marked done, wherever you tick it (the note, the Actions page, a reply). Un-tick it and the line comes back
A search box on Actions, Today, Risks, Issues, Decisions, People and Trash narrows the rows as you type. It looks at the text, the person, the category, the date and the note an action came from

Pinning now has two kinds. Pin (the P key, or right-click) keeps a page at the top of its own notebook. Pin everywhere (Shift + P, or right-click) shows it at the top of every notebook and of the notebook list. Pages you had pinned before are now pinned to their own notebook; promote the ones you want everywhere
The page list on the left shows just the title, with the date and time below it. The description line and the “0/3 done” counts are gone

Notebooks can have a category (Manage notebooks). New pages made in the notebook, or moved into it, get that category, so the actions in them can be filtered by it. When you set it, the app asks whether to apply it to the pages already there that have no category

changelog.title: Quick add anywhere, Inbox notebook, cleaner Actions and Today
items: Ctrl + Q opens Quick add from anywhere, including while you are typing in a note. The action it makes is on its own, not linked to the note you are in

New notes made when you are not inside a notebook now land in an Inbox notebook (created for you) instead of whichever notebook you used last, so they cannot get lost. Inside a notebook, new notes still go in that notebook
A new note or action that you leave without typing anything is no longer kept: empty untitled ones disappear when you move on (and the empty ones already in your file are cleared when it opens)
Actions page: the add box now has a Note button, so you can write a note on the action while creating it
Actions page: a Clear all filters link appears whenever any filter is on. A newly added action also clears a person or notebook filter that would have hidden it

Actions page: typing @Sam (or “assign to Sam”) now always assigns, even with Auto-detect dates switched off. A line under the add box shows what it will pick up, and tells you when dates are being ignored because Auto-detect dates is off, with a button to turn it on
Today: On your timeline now comes first, above Past due, and is sorted by start date

changelog.title: Fix: a note could be overwritten by the one you just left, and earlier versions
items: Fixed the cause of a note being replaced by the text and actions of the note you had just been typing in. When the page moved to another note while the old note's editor still had the cursor in it, the old note's text was written into the new one. Edits and the action-sync now only ever go to the note the editor on screen belongs to

New: the app keeps a snapshot of all your notes in this browser every few minutes, plus one before an import or before you accept a reply. Settings > Earlier versions shows them. Pick a time, see which pages differ from now, and restore any page as a copy (or download that whole version). Nothing is ever overwritten by a restore

changelog.title: Fix: copied notes sharing action items
items: Fixed a serious problem: when a note was duplicated, or its lines were copied into another note, the two notes ended up sharing the same hidden IDs for their action items. In lists like Actions and Today, changing an action from the second note then changed the one in the first note, which looked like one note overwriting another. Note names were never the cause
Duplicating a note, importing a copy, restoring from the Trash and copying tagged lines between notes now always give the new note its own action items

When you open your file, any notes that already share action IDs are repaired automatically (the older note keeps its IDs, the newer one gets new ones). A message tells you how many were fixed. If an action in the older note was changed by mistake, its earlier text can be recovered from your OneDrive version history of the save file

changelog.title: Roomier action items on small screens
items: Action items under a note (and the RAID rows) now keep their text on its own full line, with the date, time, category, assignee and repeat on a line below it. On a wide window they stay beside the text as before
A Details line under each page title folds the date, time, category and other fields away, and shows the main ones in a short summary. It is remembered

changelog.title: New-note defaults, RAID type words, hide completed
items: A new note starts with today's date and the nearest half hour (3:43 becomes 3:30, 3:45 becomes 4:00). Those are only a starting point: the note is not treated as a meeting, and does not show a date in the list, until you change the date or time yourself. The Meeting entry in the + menu still makes a real meeting

In the RAID box under a note, start the item with Risk, Issue, Decision or Action (with or without a colon, any capitals) and it becomes that type, with the word taken off the text. Before, everything became an Action
RAID (and Action items) under a note has a Hide completed switch, remembered between visits, that tucks away the finished items and says how many are hidden

changelog.title: Remembers where you were, pinned pages, date filter, Settings
items: Notes now remembers where you left off: click away to Actions or Today and back, and you are in the same notebook, on the same page. It also survives closing the app. ‹ Notebooks takes you up to the list
Pinned pages show at the top of the Notes list and at the top of every notebook, whichever notebook they belong to. Pin and unpin from the right-click menu as before

Find notes by date: on Notes there is now a date filter (Edited, Created or Page date; Today, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, This month or a custom range). Searching also matches dates, like 2026-10-12 or Oct 12
New Settings page (⚙ in the sidebar) with your save file, backup, theme and keyboard shortcuts. The sidebar bottom is now just the version, Refresh and Settings
Fixed: every page in a notebook after the first showed the notebook name beside its date

changelog.title: Replies to shared pages
items: Shared pages can now be answered. Someone (Claude, or a coworker) writes a small reply file next to the shared page file. About every 20 seconds, and whenever you come back to the app, it looks for new ones

A reply shows as a 💬 on the page and a bar at the top of the page. Review opens it: their message, then each proposed change with Accept and Reject buttons, or Accept all. Nothing in your notes changes until you accept

A reply can propose: ticking a checkbox line or an action, adding an action, changing an action's due date or owner, adding text at the end of the page, or replacing a piece of text (you see the old and new wording)
Every reply and decision is kept in a History list with the page: who wrote it, what it said, who accepted or rejected each change, and when. The author's name comes from the file and is not verified
The shared file now lists which changes you accepted or rejected, and describes how to write a reply, so whoever reads it knows what is done
Share menus have a new Check for replies now

changelog.title: Notebooks first, custom numbering, dated checkboxes
items: Notes now opens a list of your notebooks. Click one to see only its pages, and use ‹ Notebooks to go back. Searching still looks through every notebook
Pages show the title across the full row, with the date and time on the line below it

Custom numbering: ＃ Numbering… in the toolbar starts a numbered list with any prefix and starting number (for example EAM_5). Enter continues it (EAM_6, EAM_7…), Enter on an empty one ends it, and Renumber fixes the numbers after you insert a line
Ticking a checkbox in a note records the date it was completed

changelog.title: Checkboxes, a better divider, and RAID labels
items: Checkboxes inside notes: a ☐ Checkbox button in the toolbar, or type [] at the start of a line. Click the box to tick it (the line is struck through), Enter makes the next checkbox, and Enter on an empty one ends the list
Divider: typing on the line right below it now stays below it, and the divider is thicker and in the accent color so it's easy to see
The "Action items" heading under a note is now "RAID", and plain actions get their own ACTION tag at the start, like the Risk, Issue and Decision tags

changelog.title: Share a whole notebook to a folder
items: Share a whole notebook to a folder (right-click its heading → Share notebook to a folder…, or ⇪ in ⚙ Manage): every page gets its own file in a folder named after the notebook, plus a small _index.json listing the pages and when each was last edited
New pages in a shared notebook are shared automatically, and files for deleted or moved pages are removed
Sharing options per notebook: write now, choose a different folder, stop sharing, or stop and delete the files

changelog.title: Share a page to a folder
items: Share a single page to a folder on your computer (for example this project folder): the app keeps one file for that page up to date every time you edit it, with the page, its action items and a readable version of it, so it can be read by someone you point at the folder

A Share button on every note, a ⇪ marker in the list, a status badge (written at …, or paused if the browser needs you to allow the folder again), and options to write now, change the folder, or stop sharing (and delete the file)

changelog.title: Export and import notebooks
items: Export a single notebook (right-click its heading → Export notebook…, or from ⚙ Manage) as a notebook file, one Markdown file, or a PDF

Import a notebook file into any copy of the app (⤒ Import above the Notes list): new pages are added, newer edits update what you have, and nothing is deleted. Handy for moving a notebook between computers
You can also import a notebook out of a full backup file

changelog.title: Category names no longer cut off
items: The category box on action items (in notes and on the Actions page) is wide enough for names with "(inherited)", and hovering it shows the full text

changelog.title: One toggle for folding notebooks
items: Collapse all and Expand all are now a single button that switches between the two

changelog.title: Highlight color is a dropdown
items: Highlight colors are in a dropdown instead of a row of swatches, with a 🖍 button that reuses the last color you picked (click the same color on the text again to take it off)

changelog.title: People across RAID, and better highlighting
items: People: clicking someone in the sidebar now shows everything assigned to them on one page, with Actions, Risks, Issues and Decisions in their own sections, and the counts include RAID items

Highlighting: click a color swatch to highlight the selected text, click the same swatch on the text again to take it off (no more Clear), five colors to choose from, and highlighted text is always dark so it stays readable
Font color: the old Colour menu is now Font color (red, orange, green, blue, purple, gray), and picking the same color again removes it

changelog.title: Reorder notebooks, and version tracking
items: Reorder notebooks: drag a notebook heading onto another, use the ▲ ▼ buttons in ⚙ Manage, or right-click a heading → Move up / Move down
Version number in the sidebar footer, a What's new list, and a check that compares this copy with your live site and lists what the live site is missing

changelog.title: Cleaner Notes and Today
items: Today shows only actions, risks, issues, decisions and timeline items (notes no longer appear there)
The Notes tab no longer has Work / Personal / Admin category chips
Tag a line with ACTION, RISK, ISSUE or DECISION in CAPITALS without a colon (a colon still works in any capitalisation)
Pressing Enter after a tagged line keeps your cursor on the new line, and the new line doesn't copy the highlight
Deleting a notebook refreshes the list straight away, can be undone, and explains why the last notebook can't be deleted
If a file loses its notebooks (an older copy saved over it), they are restored from this browser's saved copy

changelog.title: Notebooks
items: Notebooks: the Notes list is split into colored, collapsible notebook sections
Drag pages between notebooks, use the Notebook dropdown on a note, or right-click a page
Rename, recolor and delete notebooks (right-click a heading, or ⚙ Manage)
Filter Actions and the RAID pages by notebook

changelog.title: RAID log and richer notes
items: Lines starting ACTION:, RISK:, ISSUE: or DECISION: in a note become their own entries, highlighted in the note, with a due date and @person picked up from the text
Risks, Issues and Decisions pages under RAID log, and a Scan my notes button for older notes
Text sizes, highlight colors and foldable bullets in notes
Sidebar order is Today, Actions, Notes, Timeline; meetings are just notes

changelog.title: Assignees and one kind of action
items: Assign actions to people: Assigned to box, People list, @name detection in the text, Only mine on Today
Tasks and action items are now both just actions, and the separate Tasks and Everything views are gone
Fixed time ordering on Today and Actions (finished items last, untimed after timed)

changelog.title: Today, quick add and everyday tools
items: Today view with past due and today highlighted
Quick add (Q): type it the way you'd say it
Pin to top, keyboard shortcuts with a cheat sheet (?), light / dark / auto theme
Export a note as Markdown, text or PDF; Trash that keeps deleted items for 30 days
Refresh button, tables in notes, right-click menus on lists, Actions, Today and the Timeline

changelog.title: Timeline
items: Timeline planning calendar: blocks that span days or weeks, month, 8-week and week views, Mon–Fri
Not planned yet tray, Due dates layer, recurring blocks, block descriptions, category filter

changelog.title: Formatting, groups and the installable app
items: Note formatting: bold, underline, bullets, numbers, indent, headings, links
Type chips and a shared filter bar; due-date groups (Past due, Today, Tomorrow, Later this week, …)
Installable as an app (PWA) via the site folder; long titles wrap

changelog.title: Actions and dates
items: Actions tab, due dates and categories
Dates, times and repeats found in the text ("by Friday 3pm", "every Monday")
Notes on action items, minimizable sidebars, meetings merged into notes

changelog.title: The first version
items: Tasks, notes and meetings saved automatically to a JSON file on your computer, with a red banner if saving stops
Search, tags, categories and backup
